clue.text: Branch of science reduces him to hysterics

indicators.note: to reduce someone to a state breaks them down, so the following words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Some field of study is so baffling that it leaves a man in fits of hysterics.
explanation.definitionFit: Histochemistry is the study of the chemical makeup of tissues, a recognised branch of science.

clue.text: Locksmiths?

parts.note: read not as people who fit door locks but as craftspeople who work on locks of hair

explanation.definitionFit: Hair stylists cut and shape locks of hair, so they are whimsically smiths of locks.

clue.text: Tramp in Kent possibly getting protection against bacteria?

parts.note: Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
a bum is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A vagrant in a southern English county finds some defence against germs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebum, the skin's oily secretion, has antibacterial properties, hence the question mark on this loose description.

clue.text: Provision of guns etc outside current law

indicators.note: the military supplies word sits outside, wrapping around the symbol for current

parts.note: ordnance is military supplies, especially artillery and ammunition
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A rule is being made about supplying weapons outside the current legal framework.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or regulation, especially a local by-law.

clue.text: Persists with attitude of moral recklessness?

definitions.meaning: to hang in is to persevere doggedly
read as '...', the attitude of someone who says to hell with wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going while taking a cavalier line on morality.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging in means hanging on and persevering; split differently it dismisses sin as not worth worrying about.

clue.text: Man with his book cut — dull introduction

indicators.note: the dull word comes as the introduction, standing in front of the word for cut

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A man's book is cut, with a boring opening chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew is a man who has a book named after him, the first Gospel of the New Testament.

clue.text: Clear and concise expression of desire for a good man after death?

parts.note: ST, abbreviation for saint, is the crossword's stock good man
RIP, short for 'rest in peace', is the brief wish said for someone after death

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a short, plain phrase wishing a virtuous man well once he has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'for a' and 'after death?' tie RIP to the saint: it is the abbreviated wish for a good man once he has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a room or surface is to clear it of its contents or covering.

clue.text: River rose, spawning a lake maybe

indicators.note: spawning produces something new, so the letters of the two words generate a fresh word

explanation.surface: A river's level rose and created a lake, perhaps with fish spawning in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial store of water, often a lake formed behind a dam.

clue.text: Claim of education graduate being put down

parts.note: the claim made is 'I'm', as in someone stating what they are
a B.Ed is a Bachelor of Education degree holder

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about having a teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbed, a variant spelling of embed, is to set something firmly down into a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Fail to appear to sanction

parts.note: failing to do something is not doing it
to arise is to appear or come into being

explanation.surface: Someone does not show up to give official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To notarise a document is to have a notary certify it, giving it formal approval.

clue.text: American dopes lie on the sheets in this

definitions.text: American dopes lie on the sheets in this

parts.words: American dopes lie on the sheets in this
parts.note: read not as drugged Americans in bed but as an American-spelt book whose pages list drugs

explanation.surface: Drugged-up Americans are lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacopeia, the US spelling, is an official book listing medicinal drugs on its pages.

clue.text: I am multi-dimensional, involved with Oxford University primarily — a legend in that establishment

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed together
primarily picks the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being complex, mixed up with Oxford University, where they are something of a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' means a motto or inscription, not a famous person; this Latin phrase, 'The Lord is my light', is Oxford University's motto. 'involved' mixes I AM MULTIDIMENSIONAL with OU.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend can be an inscription or motto, and this Latin phrase is the motto of Oxford University.

clue.text: The Pope imbibes a drink — not much

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in drink, so the Pope's letters take the other pieces inside

parts.note: HH stands for His Holiness, the Pope's title
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: The Pontiff takes a little sip of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha'porth, a halfpennyworth, means a tiny amount, as in 'not a ha'porth of difference'.

clue.text: One responsible for others losing their marbles

definitions.text: One responsible for others losing their marbles

parts.words: One responsible for others losing their marbles
parts.note: read not as someone driving people mad but as a man who took away a nation's marble sculptures

explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon sculptures from Athens, so Greece lost its marbles to Britain.

clue.text: Safety barrier for people on flight?

definitions.text: Safety barrier for people on flight?

parts.words: Safety barrier for people on flight?
parts.note: people on a flight sound like air passengers, but the flight is a flight of stairs with a protective rail

explanation.definitionFit: A guardrail is a protective rail, such as one along a staircase, to stop people falling.

clue.text: What offers phony rule now crawling around highest social classes?

definitions.text: What offers phony rule now crawling around highest social classes?

indicators.note: crawling around suggests wrapping oneself about something, so the jumbled letters surround the classes
phony means fake, so the letters of rule now are faked into a new order

parts.note: A and B are the top grades in British social classification

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at a party that offers sham government by fawning over the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phony' scrambles RULE NOW into NEWLOUR, and 'crawling around' puts AB inside it; the whole clue is the satirist's description of the Blair-era party.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics of Tony Blair's rebranded Labour Party accused it of spin and courting the wealthy.

clue.text: Raise hand — foul in extra time

indicators.note: foul means corrupted or messed up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A player raises a hand after a foul in extra time of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra time' suggests sport, but it is the second month of Adar added to the Jewish calendar in a leap year.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar Sheni is the extra month inserted in a Jewish leap year, literally additional time in the calendar.

clue.text: Catcher of fish lives in a ménage à trois maybe

definitions.meaning: a member of a fishing crew who takes a share of the catch

definitions.text: lives in a ménage à trois maybe
definitions.meaning: read as '...', what someone in a three-way relationship might do

explanation.surface: A fisherman lives in an unconventional three-person household.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharesman is a fishing-boat crewman paid with a share of the catch rather than wages.

clue.text: Revolutionary greeting in foreign language

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A rebel says hello in a tongue from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathi is an Indian language spoken mainly in the state of Maharashtra.

clue.text: Country province with old people half fading away

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

indicators.note: half of the word fading away leaves only its front half standing

parts.note: geriatrics are elderly people

explanation.surface: A rural region where half the elderly population is dying out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: A troublesome thing — common abbreviation for "large" not in Chambers

indicators.note: the abbreviation is not in the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a trial is a source of trouble or annoyance
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A complaint that a common abbreviation is missing from the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers looks like the dictionary, but it is the definition: heart chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are chambers, especially the upper chambers of the heart.

clue.text: Between two rivers bring out a connecting pipe

indicators.note: the word for bring out goes between the two river letters

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river, given twice
to educe is to draw out or elicit

explanation.surface: Someone lays a pipe linking two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reducer is a pipe fitting that connects two pipes of different diameters.

clue.text: Endless amusement with fabulous bird turning up on that holiday island

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed bird sits on top of the other piece
in a down clue, turning up reads the bird upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word for amusement

parts.note: fun is amusement

explanation.surface: A holiday resort where fun is endless and an exotic bird turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Brutal interrogators in exploit by a river

parts.note: a gest is a heroic deed or exploit
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: Thugs carry out their questioning beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo were the Nazi secret police, notorious for brutal interrogation.

clue.text: Man will pursue a treasure-promising sign — that's taken for granted

indicators.note: the island follows on behind, chasing the earlier letters

parts.note: X marks the spot on a treasure map
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man follows a sign that promises buried treasure, assuming it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, the Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident principle accepted as true without proof.

clue.text: Strangler with soldiers going around in band

indicators.note: the turned soldiers are placed inside the band

parts.note: a garter is an elastic band worn round the leg

indicators.note: going around turns the soldiers' letters back the other way

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A killer turns out to be among troops in a military band.
explanation.definitionFit: A garroter kills by strangling, traditionally with a cord or wire.

clue.text: Some of the literati?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A question about a select few among the intelligentsia.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top group, as the literati are among intellectuals.

clue.text: See 11
